Question B-006-007-008.

Why the correct answer is right: A vertical mobile whip radiates vertical polarization. A vertical ground-plane receiving antenna has matching polarization, so it normally receives the very-high-frequency (VHF) mobile signal best.

Why the distractors are wrong:
- sourceIndex 1: "random length of wire": A random wire has unknown impedance, pattern, and polarization, so it is not the best matched receiving choice for a vertically polarized VHF mobile signal.
- sourceIndex 2: "horizontal ground-plane antenna": A horizontal receiving antenna is cross-polarized to the vertical whip signal, even if it is described as a ground-plane arrangement.
- sourceIndex 3: "horizontal dipole antenna": A horizontal dipole is cross-polarized relative to a vertical whip, so it normally receives a weaker signal than a vertical antenna.
